name: Citizenship by Marriage to a Tanzanian Man

requirements.blocker_text: A woman married to a Tanzanian citizen may apply for naturalization at any time during her husband's lifetime, under a streamlined procedure that eliminates the standard residency requirement and the security-committee interviews required of ordinary naturalization applicants (Citizenship Act 1995, Section 11(1)). It is still a naturalization application, not automatic acquisition -- the USD 1,500 fee applies, and no equivalent streamlined provision exists for a foreign man married to a Tanzanian woman, who must instead qualify under ordinary naturalization (see tz_citizenship_naturalisation.json) with its full residency and interview requirements.
requirements.fix_path: Apply for naturalization under Section 11(1) as the wife of a Tanzanian citizen; no minimum residency or security-committee interview applies.

sources.title: Embassy of Tanzania, Washington D.C. -- lists 'Naturalization for Married Women' as a distinct provision under Section 11(1): a woman married to a Tanzanian citizen may apply at any point during the marriage without the residency requirement or security-committee interviews that apply to ordinary naturalization

notes: NEW COUNTRY BUILD (Tanzania). STATUS: PUBLISHED -- direct official-embassy sourcing, tier 1. GENDERED FINDING, CONSISTENT WITH THE PATTERN SEEN REPEATEDLY IN THIS DATASET: this streamlined route exists ONLY for a foreign wife of a Tanzanian man; a foreign husband of a Tanzanian woman gets no marriage-based fast-track at all and must qualify under ordinary naturalization on the same terms as any other unrelated applicant (12 months' immediate residence, 7 of the preceding 10 years, Kiswahili/English proficiency, good character, demonstrated contribution, newspaper notice, and district/regional security-committee interviews). Unlike Lebanon's equivalent provision, this route is still explicitly an APPLICATION for naturalization (not automatic acquisition upon request) -- the distinguishing feature here is which requirements are waived (residency, interviews), not whether ministerial/administrative discretion is removed entirely; this build did not find a source confirming or denying discretion is exercised in practice. dual_citizenship_allowed set false per the same Section 7 renunciation requirement noted in tz_citizenship_by_descent.json.
